title: SpaceX to attempt Starship catch on next flight, with eye on rapid cadence increase
gist: On its earnings call SpaceX framed itself as a data company targeting up to 10 GW of ground compute in 2027, while Musk said Starship flight 15 in November will attempt catches of both stages and cadence could reach weekly in 1H 2027 and twice weekly in 2H 2027, a claim Ars treats as typically hyper-optimistic.

insights.claim: SpaceX officials spent most of the earnings call on plans to roll out up to 10 GW of compute on the ground in 2027, with talk of Mars settlement gone and the company described as largely a data company.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: SpaceX is being valued and managed as an AI-infrastructure story, not a space-transport one.
insights.locator: In its current iteration, SpaceX is largely a data company

insights.claim: SpaceX's long-term plan to provide data services from space, first via Starlink and eventually the Starmind data center constellation, still depends on Starship as the launch vehicle.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Starship cadence is the gating factor for orbital data-center ambitions.

insights.claim: In 2027 SpaceX will largely fly its own payloads on Starship, including Starlink V3 satellites for direct-to-cell service and Starmind data center prototypes.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Starship's near-term manifest is internal, so external launch revenue is not the driver.
insights.locator: SpaceX will largely focus on its own payloads

insights.claim: Musk said SpaceX has enough data from the largely successful 14th flight to attempt catching both the Super Heavy booster and Starship upper stage on flight 15, targeted for November, and called success more likely than not.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: A first dual catch would be a major reusability milestone; watch the November flight.
insights.locator: One of the big hurdles is regulatory

insights.claim: Shotwell expects the FAA license for flight 15 to include return to launch site and tower catch for both stages, a regulatory hurdle because the vehicle must return over land including northern Mexico.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: FAA licensing timing determines whether the November date holds.
insights.quote: We have had significant constructive engagement with the FAA, and we expect the license for our Flight 15 to include return to launch site and tower catch for both stages

insights.claim: Musk expects Starship to reach a weekly flight cadence in the first half of 2027 and twice-weekly in the second half, contingent on solving rapid and complete reusability.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Ars notes Musk often gives hyper-optimistic timeframes, so discount cadence targets.
insights.quote: The rate at which we launch Starship will increase dramatically as we solve rapid and complete reusability

insights.claim: Complete reusability of an orbital rocket has never been done, so SpaceX engineering will face significant hurdles, though Ars expects them to get close over time.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Execution risk on refurbishment-free turnaround is the key swing factor on cadence.

insights.claim: SpaceX plans to refly a Starship upper stage early next year and complete the long-delayed Starship-to-Starship refueling test early in 2027.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Refueling demonstration is a prerequisite for NASA's Artemis lunar landing plans.
insights.locator: As for what comes after this test flight

insights.claim: The refueling test will produce data on transfer efficiency and boil-off of liquid oxygen and methane, which will set how many launches a Starship Moon landing for NASA's Artemis program requires.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Launch-count estimates drive Artemis cost and schedule.
insights.locator: Refueling on this scale has never been done before

insights.claim: Neither Musk nor Shotwell addressed, nor were asked by financial analysts about, the controversial throttling of Starlink capabilities for Ukraine during the earnings call.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Analysts are not pressing on geopolitical reputational risk to Starlink.
